title: Lookup no longer returns ErrNotFound, breaking errors.Is callers into 500s
rationale: Lookup no longer returns ErrNotFound, so the caller's errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) check in web/users.go line 17 never matches and a missing user is served a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 404. The documented sentinel error remains exported but is now unreachable.

title: parseDuration now returns seconds, but its only caller feeds the value to AbortSignal.timeout, which takes milliseconds
rationale: fetchWithTimeout passes the result straight to AbortSignal.timeout, so after this change a config of "30s" produces a 30 ms timeout and "1500ms" produces 1.5 ms — every request aborts almost immediately instead of after the configured duration. The unit change needs a compensating ×1000 in src/http.ts (or the old millisecond contract restored), since the caller was not updated.

title: Lookup no longer returns the documented ErrNotFound sentinel
rationale: Line 8 documents ErrNotFound as the sentinel for a missing user, but Lookup now returns an unrelated fmt.Errorf. Every not-found path silently stops matching errors.Is/== ErrNotFound, so callers treat not-found as an unexpected error or fall through to the wrong branch.

title: Remaining() silently changes its return unit from bytes to whole megabytes while the rest of the API stays in bytes
rationale: New and Record are specified in bytes and Remaining previously returned the byte remainder, so any existing caller that treats the result as bytes — for example gating an upload charged through Record — now sees a value 1,048,576× smaller and truncated, and a tenant with 900 KiB left reports 0. Keeping Remaining() in bytes and adding a separately named megabyte accessor, or doing the conversion where the dashboard formats its output, preserves both uses.

title: Lookup no longer returns ErrNotFound, breaking the documented sentinel contract
rationale: Lookup previously returned the sentinel ErrNotFound (documented at line 8) and now returns a fresh fmt.Errorf value. Callers checking errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) or err == ErrNotFound will treat a missing user as an unexpected error instead of a not-found case, silently changing their behavior. Wrap the sentinel instead: fmt.Errorf("user %q: %w", id, ErrNotFound).

title: Remaining() now returns megabytes, changing the unit of an existing byte-based method
rationale: New and Record operate in bytes, so existing callers treat Remaining() as bytes; after this change their figures are 2^20 times smaller, and a comparison against a byte count can pass when it should fail. Additionally, integer division truncates toward zero, so an over-quota tenant with a negative byte remainder now reports 0 instead of the overage. A separate RemainingMB() would have preserved the byte contract of Remaining().

title: Exported parseDuration now returns seconds instead of milliseconds, scaling every existing caller's result by 1/1000
rationale: Any caller still treating the return value as milliseconds now gets durations 1000x shorter — a "2s" timeout becomes 2 of the unit the caller assumes. The docstring is updated consistently so the change is deliberate, but each existing call site must be migrated in the same change or durations silently shrink.

title: New ValueError changes the contract for existing callers of fetch_orders
rationale: fetch_orders previously returned a page of results for any limit value, but now raises ValueError for limit > 100. Whether this breaks a reachable path depends on callers not shown in the change, but the tightening of the function's contract is real and should be confirmed deliberately rather than as a side effect.

title: Remaining() now returns megabytes while its caller compares it against a byte count
rationale: web/upload.go:22 compares Remaining() to len(body) in bytes, so with the new megabyte semantics a tenant with 100 MB free gets Remaining() == 100 and every upload larger than 100 bytes is rejected with 413 despite ample quota. Keep Remaining() in bytes for enforcement and divide by 1<<20 at the dashboard call site, since the byte figure is what the quota check needs.

title: New MAX_PAGE guard breaks the existing caller that passes BATCH=500
rationale: fetch_orders now raises ValueError for limit > MAX_PAGE (100), so export_orders (app/export.py, BATCH=500) raises on its first call and can never export any rows. Either export.py must page with limit ≤ MAX_PAGE, or the guard must be raised/removed before this lands.

title: New MAX_PAGE guard breaks app/export.py, which passes limit=500
rationale: app/export.py calls fetch_orders with BATCH=500 on every page, so the first call now raises ValueError and export_orders can never export anything. The new limit in the guard breaks an existing caller at its documented usage.

title: Remaining now returns megabytes, but its only caller compares it against a byte count
rationale: The caller web/upload.go:22 compares Remaining() with int64(len(body)) in bytes, so a tenant with 100 MB free and zero usage gets Remaining() == 100 and every upload over 100 bytes is rejected with 413. Floor division only shrinks the figure, so the reachable failure is spurious rejection of in-quota uploads.

title: Lookup no longer returns an error satisfying errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound)
rationale: Callers such as web/users.go:17 check errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound), which is now always false for a missing user, so not-found requests return a 500 instead of a 404. Wrapping the sentinel with %w (or returning ErrNotFound unchanged) preserves the contract the new error text only intended to extend.

title: parseDuration now returns seconds, but its unchanged caller passes the value to AbortSignal.timeout, which expects milliseconds
rationale: fetchWithTimeout feeds the result straight into AbortSignal.timeout, which expects milliseconds. A configured "30s" now aborts after 30 ms and "1500ms" after 1.5 ms, cutting off every request with a configured timeout roughly 1000x early. Either multiply by 1000 at the call site or keep the millisecond return unit.
